title: The blues drum beat and Mississippi riverboat bands at Memphis
summary: Crawford recalls hearing riverboat bands with blues trumpets and trombones from the Memphis levee.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Now, could you -- going back to the subject that you had about blues playing, do you recall the way that the blues beat developed for the drums?
When I was -- pardon me, Stanley, but

I was raised in a blues town, Memphis. And places like that, where the riverboats used to come through by Memphis, went through on the Mississippi River. And you had bands on there that you could stand on (the) levee, and you'd listened to those trumpets and those old slide trombones. Trumpets would be punctuating the air with blues. That's all they had in their minds, blues. Everything that they had played consisted of some kind of blues. (Singing.)

That kind of stuff. Oh, you had to have it in you. You couldn't get a symphonic (guy to come and out of) -- play that kind of stuff. Colored people, boy, they contributed more than a lot of people realized, and admit that they contributed. They did the thing, when it come to that soul music and soul food, that kind of stuff, you just can't beat them.
